cues.text: On February 3, 1822, Septuagesima Sunday, at the Church of St. Eulalia in Bordeaux, France, Abbot Delort substituted for Father Pierre Bienvenu Noailles.
Noailles had founded the religious community of the Holy Family of Bordeaux twenty months earlier.
Delort exposed the Blessed Sacrament for adoration and gave the customary blessing with the monstrance.

Immediately afterward, those present reported that Jesus appeared within the Host itself: a young man of about thirty, his head, chest, and arms visible as though in a living portrait, wearing a dark red scarf draped over one shoulder.
Abbot Delort called the altar server over, who confirmed he could see the same figure.
The apparition lasted more than twenty minutes, witnessed by a large number of the faithful gathered for the service.

Those present described the figure's head moving gently from side to side, a smile crossing his face, and his right hand raised in blessing over the congregation; one witness later reported having heard the words, "I am He who is."
The event was reported to Archbishop d'Aviau of Bordeaux, who personally heard the testimony of the faithful who had witnessed it and gave the account his approval.
The relic monstrance associated with the apparition is preserved today at Martillac, France, in the church of the contemplative community known as La Solitude.
The community Father Noailles had founded only twenty months before the apparition, the Holy Family of Bordeaux, remains active today.

It has a particular presence in Asia and Africa, carrying forward in its ordinary daily life the same devotion its members witnessed unfold before them on an otherwise ordinary Sunday in February 1822.
The Chapel of the Miracle in Bordeaux remains open to visitors who wish to see, in the same building, where twenty minutes once held an entire congregation in wonder.
